CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steve Talt, Mayor  www.CityofSanMarino.org
Steven W. Huang, DDS, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Tony Chou, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 13, 2023 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626) 300-0705 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.CityofSanMarino.org/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org until
  3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will
  be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00

   p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council
  at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us
  teleconference module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted
  after the in-person comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to
read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First
Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require
having the title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or
resolution be read in its entirety before taking any action.

   CEREMONIAL

 PRESENTATION OF CITY TILE TO, AND REMARKS FROM, OUTGOING
 MAYOR STEVE TALT

 REORGANIZATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL BY SELECTING A MAYOR AND
 VICE MAYOR

 REMARKS FROM THE NEWLY APPOINTED MAYOR

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

 1.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-23-31 ADOPTING THE COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROJECT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council conduct a public hearing to
  consider the use of CDBG funds for the Senior Outreach Program and ADA compliant
  Sidewalk Replacement Program in FY 2024-25. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, the appropriate motion, after the hearing, would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-23-31, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of San Marino, California adopting the projected use of funds from the Community
  Development Block Grant program for Fiscal Year 2024-25.”

  NEW BUSINESS

 2.  RECEIVE AND FILE FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FIRST QUARTER (JULY
  2023 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 2023)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the financial report reflecting the City’s revenues and
  expenditures as of September 30, 2023.”

 3.  RECEIVE AND FILE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT
  (ANNUAL AUDIT) FOR THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that this annual financial statement be received
  and filed. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the audited financial statements for the fiscal year ended
  June 30, 2023.”

AGENDA – DECEMBER 13, 2023  PAGE 3 of 7
   CONSENT CALENDAR

 4.  APPROVAL OF CONTRACT FOR IT  CONSULTING/MANAGEMENT
  SERVICES WITH SDI PRESENCE, LLC

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve a three-year
  professional services agreement with an option to extend the contract for two more
  years with SDI Presence, LLC for Information Technology Consulting/Management
  Services. If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion
  would be:

  “I move to approve a three-year professional services agreement with an option to
  extend the contract for two more years with SDI Presence, LLC for Information
  Technology Consulting/Management Services and authorize the City Manager to
  exercise the future option under the contract in his discretion, subject to satisfactory
  performance and Council budget appropriation.”

 5.  APPROVAL OF PURCHASE FOR FIRE DEPARTMENT SELF-CONTAINED
  BREATHING APPARATUS AND FILL STATION

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council waive competitive bidding and (1)
  approve the purchase of 3M Scott self-contained breathing apparatus from Allstar
  Fire Equipment in the amount of $224,238.28; and (2) approve the purchase of a
  Stallion Air Centaur fill station from L.N. Curtis in the amount of $82,686.39. If the
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to waive competitive bidding and (1) approve the purchase of 3M Scott self-
  contained breathing apparatus from Allstar Fire Equipment in the amount of
  $224,238.28; and (2) approve the purchase of a Stallion Air Centaur fill station from
  L.N. Curtis in the amount of $82,686.39.”

 6.  APPROVAL OF PURCHASE OF ONE POLICE VEHICLE FROM NATIONAL
  AUTO FLEET IN THE AMOUNT OF $64,810.58

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the purchase of one
  Police Department vehicle from National Auto Fleet in the amount of $64,810.58.

  “I move to approve the purchase of one Police Department vehicle from National
  Auto Fleet in the amount of $64,810.58.”

 7.  APPROVAL  TO  PROCURE  AND  INSTALL  NEW  IRRIGATION
  CONTROLLERS FOR LACY PARK IN THE AMOUNT OF $43,595

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the procurement and
  installation of two irrigation controllers from Imperial Sprinkler Supply in the amount
  of $43,595.

  “I move to approve the procurement and installation of two irrigation controllers from
  Imperial Sprinkler Supply in the amount of $43,595.”

AGENDA – DECEMBER 13, 2023  PAGE 4 of 7
  8.  APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ATLAS
  PLANNING SOLUTIONS FOR LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN
  PREPARATION SERVICES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve a professional services
  agreement with Atlas Planning Solutions for Local Hazard Mitigation Plan preparation
  services. If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion
  would be:

  “I move to approve a professional services agreement with Atlas Planning Solutions
  for Local Hazard Mitigation Plan preparation services.”

 9.  APPROVAL OF 2024 LACY PARK MAJOR SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT
  DATES AND CO-SPONSORSHIP REQUESTS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the 2024 Lacy Park Special
  Event Permit Dates and Fee Requests. It the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  ”I move to approve the 2024 Lacy Park Special Event Permit Dates and Co-
  Sponsorship Requests.”

 10. APPOINTMENT TO THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES OF THE GREATER LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY VECTOR CONTROL DISTRICT

  Recommendation: The Mayor recommends the Council appoint Howard Brody as the
  City’s representative to the Great Los Angeles County Vector Control District Board
  of Trustees to serve a two (2) year term. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be :

  ”I move to appoint Howard Brody to serve on the Board of Trustees for the Greater
  Los Angeles Vector Control District for a two (2) year term ending January 1, 2026.

 11. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF OCTOBER
  2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of October
  2023.”

 12. RECEIVE AND FILE  MONTHLY  DISBURSEMENTS  REPORT  FOR
  NOVEMBER 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of November 2023. If the City Council concurs
  with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

AGENDA – DECEMBER 13, 2023  PAGE 5 of 7
   “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of
  November 2023.”

 13. APPROVAL  OF  NOTICE  OF  COMPLETION  FOR  STREET
  REHABILITATION PROJECT NO. 21-9271

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council accept the street
  rehabilitation project as complete and authorize the City Clerk to file the Notice of
  Completion. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to accept Street Rehabilitation Project No. 21-9271 as complete and
  authorize the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion.”

 14. SCHEDULED VACANCIES FOR COMMISSIONS, COMMITTEES, AND
  BOARDS FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2024

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council accept and file the Local
  Appointments List for all City commissions, committees, and boards for calendar
  year 2024, and direct the City Clerk to post the list.

 15. REQUEST TO CAST VOTES FOR THE SAN GABRIEL BASIN WATER
  QUALITY AUTHORITY BOARD OF DIRECTORS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council vote in favor of Rosemead City
  Council Member Margaret Clark. If Council concurs, the appropriate action would be:

  “I move to approve the vote in favor of Rosemead City Councilmember Margaret
  Clark to the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority Board of Directors and adopt
  Resolution No. R-23-32, A Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Marino,
  California, Casting its Vote for Councilmember Margaret Clark to Represent Cities
  without Prescriptive Pumping Rights on the Board of the San Gabriel Basin Water
  Quality Authority.”

 16. WINTER 2023 PUBLIC TREE REMOVAL LIST

  Recommendation: This is an informational item. Therefore, no action is required by
  City Council.

 17. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the November 2023
  minutes. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the special meeting of November 8, 2023, and
  the regular meeting of November 8, 2023.”

AGENDA – DECEMBER 13, 2023  PAGE 6 of 7
  18. ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O-23-1409 (SECOND READING)
  ADDING  MUNICIPAL  CODE  SECTION  23.05.03 REGARDING
  DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS AND OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS
  FOR MULTI-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS IN THE
  HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL ZONE

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Ordinance No. O-23-1409. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to adopt Ordinance No. O-23-1409, an Ordinance of the San Marino City
  Council adding San Marino Municipal Code Section 23.05.03 regarding development
  standards and objective design standards for multi-family residential development
  projects in the Historical and Cultural Zone.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

ADJOURNMENT
